summary: With regard to the prayer of the Petitioner for condonation of time overrun for the period from April 2013 to January 2015, on account of violence and bandh in the concerned area/region, the Commission, in its order dated 22.5.2017 (in Petition No.45/GT/2016), held as under: _“20. As regards time over-run due to violence and bandhs during the period from April, 2013 to January, 2015, petitioner has requested to condone the delay of 671 days and has furnished the copy of the various prohibitory orders, but the same does not indicate the exact date of imposition of prohibitory orders. The petitioner has also submitted the supporting document indicating the prohibition from 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 (i.e. 32 days). Though, the petitioner was directed to submit the effective duration of bandh against prohibitory orders, the petitioner has not submitted the same and therefore, we are inclined to condone the delay of only 32 days. Based on the above discussion, the total delay of 32 days has been condoned, out of the delay of 671 days claimed by the petitioner.”_ _“18. .. Accordingly, on analysis of such prohibitory orders, the delay of 32 days (from 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014) was condoned in order dated 22.5.2017. The Commission having considered the documents furnished by the petitioner with regard to violence and bandhs while allowing the time overrun in order dated 22.5.2017, we find no reason to entertain the petitioner’s plea for review of the said order on this issue. Accordingly, there is no error apparent on the face of the order dated 22.5.2017 and therefore the prayer of the petitioner for review on this ground fails.”_ _19. Hence, the findings of the commission on this issue are absolutely erroneous and unjustified, which cannot be sustained. The same are hereby set aside. We remand the matter back to the Commission to decide the issue afresh after hearing the parties and in the light of whole bunch of documents filed by the appellant, as noted hereinabove.”_ 4. In the remand proceedings, the Petitioner, on the issue of time overrun for the period from April 2013 to January, 2015 on account of violence and Bandhs in the concerned area/region, had submitted the following: _“As regards the issue (a)-time overrun for the period from April, 2013 to January, 2015 (671 days) on account of ethnic violence and bandh in the concerned area, the Commission had refused to condone the delay for the said period, except the period of 32 days, citing non-submission of prohibitory orders by NTPC during the time period in question. However, the APTEL has held that the Commission had taken note of only one page, which bears details of Section 144 prohibitory orders enforced between 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 and thus condoned the delay of these 32 days only. Whereas, the Petitioner had provided several other documents to support its claim that the project work was seriously impeded on account of violence and bandh from April 2013 to January 2015, but the same has not been considered._ _The APTEL in para 17 of its judgment has also held that the situation in Kokrajhar District, where the power project was being constructed, remained volatile and affected by regular bandhs/curfew/prohibitory orders etc., throughout the years 2013-15, and the situation returned to normal in January 2015. The finding of APTEL is amply clear that the situation in Kokrajhar remained volatile for the complete period of the dispute (2013-15) and therefore, the delay on account of ethnic violence and bandh of 671 days, during this period, is to be condoned, considering the overlapping period”_ ## _5._ However, the Commission, after examining the aforesaid submissions, including the documents filed by the Petitioner for the said period, vide order 20.11.2025, held as under: _“27. The Petitioner has further submitted that the project construction activities were affected due to the unrest, violence, etc. caused in the Kokrajhar district, where the project is located and has also provided the documents indicating the time overrun, progress bar chart, etc., for the activities affected. As submitted by the Petitioner, due to the poor law and order situation and bandh calls, in the Kokrajhar area, the workers had not turned up for work or were available in small numbers, which had a cascading effect, as the work on all fronts came to a near halt. In addition, the movement of goods and vehicles was affected during the bandh. Also, these disturbances/law and order issues have disrupted the normal project operations, thereby leading to significant delays in the project development activities. Thus, the participation of the various groups in bandhs, resulted in_ _28. As stated, the Petitioner, in Appendix-A has also submitted a tabular statement_ _indicating the date of the prohibitory order and the period of enforcement/revocation, during the period 2013-2015, which works out to a delay of 550 days, inclusive of the delay of 32 days allowed for the period 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 vide Commission’s order dated 22.5.2017. In consideration of the above submissions and the documents available on record, we condone the total delay of 550 days (which is inclusive of the 32 days delay already allowed vide order dated 22.5.2017), for the period 2013-15, after adjusting the overlapping period, since the said delays, due to violence/riots/ incidents relating to NDBF/Bandhs and Prohibitory orders, in Kokrajhar district, were all beyond the control of the Petitioner. In other words, for the period 2013-15, an additional delay of 518 days (55032) has been allowed in this order, in terms of the submissions/documents, and based on the findings of the APTEL judgment.”_
title: Approval of tariff for Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station, Unit-I (250 MW) for the period 2016-19 - Implementation of the APTEL judgment dated 19.11.2024 in Appeal No. 137/2019 (NTPC v CERC & ors). NTPC Limited
